metadata.title: Microsoft updates on outage disrupting Outlook email, Teams, and Copilot for users

content.text:
Microsoft (MSFT) was working into Friday to restore user access to its workplace software tools, including email, after an outage that spanned multiple regions. The connectivity issues, which began Thursday, were being worked on for hours with the company at one point Thursday evening indicating that servers that had been brought back online became unresponsive again.
By Friday morning, Microsoft said it was seeing continued recovery progress across affected regions, with broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe, and encouraging recovery signals in Asia Pacific.
"Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as mitigation continues across remaining affected infrastructure," said the update on X.
On Thursday afternoon, Microsoft said users of Exchange Online, which powers Outlook email, as well as the company's Teams videoconferencing app and Copilot AI chatbot, may experience disruptions. In a separate post on X, the company said users "in any region" could be affected.
Microsoft said it was rerouting connection traffic across its global infrastructure and restarting affected servers. Around 7:05 p.m. ET, Microsoft said some servers were becoming unresponsive again as traffic returned, underscoring that the company had not yet fully stabilized the outage.
A while later, the company said it was adding capacity to handle increased traffic as more regions came back online.
Friday morning, Microsoft said, "Our focus remains on stabilizing recovered infrastructure, completing mitigation in remaining impacted areas, and reducing delayed email queues and backlogs while we validate service consistency across connection methods."
